full_judgment:
Bhabani Prasad Singha, J: This Death Reference has been made by Shahed Noor Uddin, the learned Judge, Druta Bichar Tribunal No.1, Dhaka for confirmation of the death sentence imposed upon the condemned accused-persons, namely, Md. Aiyub Ali, Salam alias Ketu Salam, Mannan shah, Faruq Gazi for killing of the deceased Hashem Kazi, the accused-persons, namely, Aiyub Ali, Kuti Chand, Sabuj Ali, Nazir, Nizam, Mahfuz son of Aiyub Ali, Ripon, Mannan Shah, Shafiul Azam Dafader, Hashem, Faruq Gazi, Abdul Mannan alias mobile Mannan, Javed Ali and Mizan for killing of the deceased-persons Manwar Ali and Badshah vide his judgment and order of conviction dated 12.07.2005 passed in Druta Bichar Tribunal Case No.06 of 2004 corresponding to G.R. Case No. 179 of 2001 and Sreenagar (Munshiganj) P.S. Case No. 10(07)2001. By the said judgment and order, the learned trial court sentenced the convict-accused-persons, namely, Kuti chand, Sabuj Ali, Nazir and Nazim to suffer imprisonment for life for killing of Hashem, sentenced the accused-persons, namely, Salam Sikder, Mahfuz son of Aiyub Ali, Mintoo, Shawkat Ali Molla, Jainal Mokter alias Jainal Abedin, Badsha, Mithu, A.Rob alias Roba and Ayesha Begum to suffer imprisonment for life for killing of the deceased Manwar Ali and Badsha, sentenced the convict-accused-persons, namely. Salam Shikder, Mahfuz son of Aiyub Ali, Mintoo, Shawkat Ali Molla, Jainal Mokter alias Jainal Abedin, Badshah, Mithu, A. Rob alias Roba for making attempt to kill the victims Anwar Ali and Salauddin and convicted the convict-accused-persons, namely, Shamsuddin, Alek, Syed Chowdhury, Ratan Chaktabarty, Rafique Sikder, Masood son of Sheikh Shahjahan, Piyar Ali, Jasim, Titon Khan, Morom Ali , Nannoo Shikder and Hossain member under section 148 of the Penal code to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 2 (two) years and to pay a fine of tk.2,000/00 each, in default, to suffer rigorous imprisonment for another 3 (three) months. 

 2. As against the impugned judgment and order, the convict-accused-persons, namely, Shafiul Azam Dafader, Mannan Shah and Abdus Salam alias Ketu Salam preferred Criminal Appeal No. 3451 of 2005, the convict- accused-persons Md. Ayub Ali Chairman, Mahfuzur Rahman alias Mahfuz, Badsha, A. Rob Bepari alias Roba, Ayesha Begum alias Ayesha Khatun, Shamsuddin, Titon Khan alias Titan Khan and Morom Ali preferred Criminal Appeal No. 3581 of 2005, the convict-accused-persons Nannoo Sikder and Rafique Sikder preferred Criminal Appeal No. 3157 of 2005, the convict- accused Md. Hashem preferred criminal Appeal No. 3354 of 2005, the convict-accused Hossain member alias Sheikh Ali preferred Criminal Appeal No. 3558 of 2005, the convict-accused Mithu preferred Criminal Appeal No. 3413 of 2005, the convict accused A. Salam alias Ketu Salam preferred Jail Appeal No. 762 of 2005, the convict-accused Shafiul Azam preferred Jail Appeal No. 763 of 2005, the convict-accused Hashem preferred Jail Appeal No. 764 of 2005, the convict-accused Md. Mahfuzur Rahman preferred Jail Appeal No. 765 of 2005, the convict-accused Md. Mannan Shall preferred Jail Appeal No. 766 of 2005, the convict-accused Aiyub Ali chairman preferred Jail Appeal No. 767 of 2005, the convict-accused Faruq Gazi preferred Jail Appeal No. 92 of 2006, the convict-accused Md. Jainal Mokter alias Jainal Abedin filed Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 12454 of 2008 under Section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the convict-accused Faruq Gazi filed Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 7729 of 2006 under Section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and the convict-accused Shawkat Ali Molla filed Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 32472 of 2011 under Section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 3. In short, the prosecution case is that on 07.07.2001 at about 8.00 a.m. the deceased Manwar Ali, his brother Md. Anwar Ali and nephew Salauddin left for Bagra Bazar. For their convenience of going to Bagra Bazar they were going through the road of Al-Amin Madrashah and along Dhaka-Dohar Road. On that way the house of the accused Aiyub Ali chairman was situated. While Manwar Ali along with his elder brother, brother-in-law and nephew of her husband was going through that road, all on a sudden, the accused-persons Aiyub Ali chairman, Nazir, Mizan and Badshah, the sons of late Swarup Ali, Sabuj Ali, Kuti Chan, Mahfuz, Mintoo, Abdul Mannan Shah, Faruq Gazi, Salam, Mithu, Alek member son of late Hossain, Selim, Billal, Ripon, Piyar Ali, Jasim, Muluk, Alek son of unknown, Shafiul Azam, Syed Chowdhury, Ayesha Khatun wife of Abu Jaher, Rubel, Maram Ali, Abdur Rob Bepari alias Roba, Keru Fakir member, Adalat Sikder, Jainal Talukder, Aynal, Haroon, Salam Sikder, Shamsuddin, Aminur Rahman, Jewel, Abdul Mannan alias Mobile Mannan, Kuddus Bepari, Akram Ali Bepari, Rouf, Faraj Sheikh, Titan Khan, Hossain member, Malek Bepari, Shah Alam Bepari, Muktar Hossain, Sekander, Ummat Ali, Mahfuz son of Salam Sikder, Amin, Israfil Bepari, Abbas, Hashem son of Hasen Gazi, Faraj Ali, Motaleb Fakir, Ketu Salam alias Kota Salam, Abdul Gazi and many unknown persons being armed with weapons like `gun'; `ramdao', `chapati', 'iron Rod', 'Chinese axe' etc. attacked them. Though the deceased Manwar Ali and his associates were carrying two licensed guns, pistol they ran towards the house of Srijon Bepari and entered into his house and started shouting "save, save". Hearing their alarm, the passersby gathered there. In the meantime, the accused Aiyub Ali and the aforesaid persons started shouting saying that "Manwar Ali chairman should be killed. He cannot be saved. After a long time we got him. It is my long cherished desire. Today I will fulfil it". Saying this, the accused Aiyub Ali chairman started firing targeting the house of Srijan Bepari. He and the aforesaid persons fired targeting the public so that they could not come forward. For that, being frightened the public went far away. Being frightened, the deceased Manwar Ali and his associates requested Srijan Bepari to give them shelter in his house. Haji Srijan Bepari being kind enough gave them shelter in his two storied wooden house and for that, the accused-persons started looting that house. For that reason Hazi Srijan Bepari and his family members went away from that house. Finding no other way the deceased Manwar Ali started blank firing from his brother's licensed gun and pistol and instructed his relatives to inform the police station over mobile phone. In the meantime, his relatives informed the police station. The reason for carrying guns and pistol by the deceased Manwar Ali and his brother is that the accused Aiyub Ali chairman and his family is their enemy. 26/27 years back the accused Aiyub Ali and his brothers took away the father of the deceased Manwar Ali from a tea-stall of Bagrabazar and cut his body into pieces and threw the pieces into the river Padma. The pieces of the body could not be found. Thereafter, they were threatening the deceased Manwar Ali and his family members and for that they used to carry their licensed guns and pistol while they had to go to Bagrabazar. A.Rob alias Roba son of late Rashid Bepari informed the accused Aiyub Ali about the deceased Manwar Ali's going to Bagra bazar on 07.07.2001. Roba is the terrorist of the accused Ayub Ali's group who was in the jail several times for his terrorist activities. Being informed by Robs the accused Aiyub Ali took preparation about which the deceased Manwar Ali was ignorant. On 07.07.2001 at 1.00 p.m. Sreenagar Thana police went to the place of occurrence and sent message to different police stations like Lowhajang, Sirajdikhan and Dohar. The Deputy Commissioner and the Police super of Munshiganj, the T.N.O. from Sreenagar went to the place of occurrence from 2.00 p.m. to 5.00 p.m. The District Magistrate; the Police Super and the O.C. Sreenagar P.S. could not bring the accused-persons under control. The deceased Manwar Ali and his companions were in confinement at the 1st floor of the Srijon Bepari's wooden house from 9.00 a.m. till their death. The deceased-persons opened frequent gun shots for their safety. At about 6.00 p.m. the District Magistrate and the Police Administration announced through a hand mike addressing Manwar Ali to come throwing down their weapons and to surrendered to them. They also announced assuring them if they surrendered to them they would save them. Hearing this, the deceased Manwar Ali along with others came down from the 1st floor of the said house. The police then arrested them out of suspicion and handcuffed them. Forthwith, the accused Aiyub Ali and other accused-persons snatched the deceased Manwar Ali and his companions away from the police custody and killed them. The accused Aiyub Ali then dealt a sharp weapon blow from the back of the deceased Manwar Ali in presence of police. At the same time, the other accused-persons,namely, Nazir, Mizan, Nizam, Badsha, Sabuj, Kuti Chan, Mahfuz, Mintoo gave indiscriminate blow with sharp cutting weapons on the ,different parts of the body of the deceased Manwar Ali. The accused Abdul Mannan Shah son of Malek Shah, Faruq Gazi, Salam, Mintoo, Alek member son of Hossain, Selim, Billal, Ripon, Piyar Ali, Jasim, Muluk, Alek son of unknown, Safiul Azam, Syed Chowdhury, Ayesha Khatun and wife of Abu Taher started dealing blows on the body of the deceased Manwar Ali with sharp cutting weapons. The accused-persons Jainal son of late Beshai Talukder, Aynal son of Joynal Talukder, Haroon, Salam Sikder, Shamsuddin, Sekander, Ummat Ali, Mahfuz son of Salam sikder, Rubel, Keru Fakir member dealt stick and iron rod blows to the brother of the deceased Manwar Ali. The accused-persons Aminur Rahman, Jewel, Abdul Mannan, started dealing blow on the body of Salauddin, the nephew of the deceased Manwar Ali. The accused-persons Aminur Rahman, Jewel, Abdul Mannan started dealing blows upon the body of Salauddin, the nephew of Manwar Ali with sharp cutting weapons. The accused-persons Kamal, Abbas, Hashim, Kuddus Bepari, Akram Ali Bepari, Rouf, Fazal Sheikh, Titan Khan, Hasen member, Malek Bepari, Sahah Alam Bepari started firing all around so that no body come forward to rescue them. The accused-persons Mukter Hossain Bepari, Motaleb Gazi, Idris, Faraj Ali, Motaleb Fakir, Hari Das, Ketu Salam alias Kota Salam, Abdul Awal Gazi, Gaffar assisted the other accused-persons with 'sticks', `ramdao', `kirich', 'teta' and `shorki' so that the people could not come forward to assist the victims. Due to the aforesaid blows the deceased Manwar Ali and Badsha died at the place of occurrence. Thereafter, police carried the dead bodies of Manwar Ali and Badsha in a police van to the police station. As the elder brother and the nephew of the deceased Manwar Ali were alive they were sent to the hospital. At about 7.00 p.m. the informant heard about the death of her husband from the witnesses and lost sense. At about 2.00 to 2.30 p.m. when the body of the deceased Manwar Ali and his brother in law was sent to the hospital for autopsy. On 08.07.2001 after completion of autopsy when their dead bodies were brought to the residence of the informant she once again lost her sense. Thereafter, their dead bodies were buried after completion of religious rituals. When the informant regained sense she heard about the wound marks of her husband, the deceased Manwar Ali from her relatives. The brother-in-law of the informant was in the hospital and other relatives were living abroad. The cause of delay in lodging the first Information Report (FIR) was that the informant lost balance of her mind because of the death of her husband. 

 7. On the closure of the evidence of the prosecution the present accused-persons, namely, Nannoo Sikder, Hossain member alias Sheikh Ali Hossain, Shamsudduin Bepari, Badsha, Morom Ali, Titon Khan, Md. Shafiul Azam alias Shafiullah, Md. Mannan Shah, Hashem, Md. Mahfuzur Rahman, Mithu, A. Salem alias Ketu Salem, Ayesha Begum, Md. Aiyub Ali Chairman were examined under Section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to which they pleaded innocence informing the tribunal that they would not adduce any evidence on their behalf. On the other hand, the other accused-persons being absconding they could not be examined under Section 342 of the code of Criminal Procedure. 

 9. At the very outset Advocate Mr. Samar Ahmed representing the convict-accused-persons Hashem Member, Mannan Shah, Salem alias Ketu Salem, Ayesha Begum, Badsha, Faruq Gazi, Jainal Mokter and Shawkat Ali Mollah submits that the FIR of the case being lodged five days after the alleged occurrence, there was every scope for embellishment in this case and that five days' delay in lodging the FIR is not explained satisfactorily; that the FIR of the instant case is not an FIR inasmuch as a GDE was made prior to the lodging of the FIR and as such, it should be treated as a statement under Section 161 of the Code of Criminal procedure; that the statements of the witnesses under Section 161 of the Code of Criminal procedure being recorded after long lapse of time the evidence of the prosecution witnesses should be left out of consideration; that the learned court below did not properly examine the accused-persons under Section 342 of the Code of Criminal procedure; that the prosecution did not examine all the witnesses named in the FIR and Charge Sheet which rendered the prosecution case doubtful; that the Sketch Map of the place of occurrence was not proved as S.I. Belayet Hossain who prepared the Sketch Map was not examined in the case; that the learned trial court had no jurisdiction to try the case as the occurrence took place prior to coming into force of Druta Bichar Ain; that the Seizure Lists in respect of the arms and ammunition are not acceptable in evidence as some of the Seizure List witnesses were not examined by the prosecution; that the prosecution case is an absurd one because it was not possible for the accused-persons to perpetrate the alleged occurrence in presence of police-personnel and officers of administration; that in the FIR save and except the accused Aiyub Ali , the overt act of the other accused-persons being not explained, the impugned judgment and order cannot be sustained; that the prosecution witnesses being interested, related and partisan their evidence cannot be relied upon; that that there being no medical evidence to show that the accused Ayesha Begum dealt brick blows to the deceased Manwar Ali, the conviction and sentence as awarded to her cannot be maintained; that the Investigating Officers of the case performed perfunctory investigation in this case and that at all events the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set aside. The learned Advocate also referred the decisions reported in 3 ADC at page 575, 12 BLC at page 165, 9 BLD at page 474, 15 BLD at page 205, 6 BCR (AD) at page 225, 38 DLR (AD) at page 311, 11 BLD (AD) at page 02, 52 DLR at page 400, 57 DLR at page 513, 15 MLR at page 311, 24 BCR at page 443, 46 DLR at page 575, 56 DLR at page 185, 10 BLC at page 69, 54 DLR (AD) at page 60 , 40 DLR (AD) at page 291, 14 BLD at page 33, 8 BLC at page 52 and 15 BLD (AD) at page 54. 

 10. Advocate Mr. Shah Manjurul Haque representing the convict-accused-persons Aiyub Ali, Mahfuzur Rahman and Shafiul Alam submits that the FIR of this case is to be treated as a statement under Section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure; that in this case specific allegation is only against the accused Aiyub Ali, not against others and as such, conviction and sentence as awarded against the other accused-persons cannot be sustained; that framing of the charge in the case is defective; that there is material discrepancy between the evidence of the pw1 and the pw4 and the doctor examined; that the accused-persons were present at the place of occurrence as the mere spectators and that they did not commit any offence as alleged; that the Investigating Officers of the case did not take out investigation of the case properly; that the impugned judgment and order is a not speaking one; that the trial court failed to comply with the mandatory provisions of Sections 10 and 13 of the Druta Bichar Ain and that the prosecution has not been able to prove the case beyond all shadow of doubt and as such, the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set aside. 

 12. Advocate Mrs. Hasna Begum, the learned State Defence Lawyer for the convict-accused-persons Kuti Chand, Sabuj Ali, Nazir, Mizan, Ripon, A, Mannan, Mintoo, Salam Sikder, Mahfuz and Javed Ali submits that the trial of the case was held in absence of the aforesaid accused-persons and that save and except their abscondence no corroborative, legal and satisfactory evidence is there to convict them; that the statements of the witnesses under Section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure being recorded after long lapse of time, the evidence of the prosecution witnesses should be discarded; that mere abscondence of an accused is not the conclusive proof of his guilt and cannot be the sole basis for his conviction. She also referred the decisions reported in 54 DLR (AD) at page 137, 55 DLR at page 160, 59 DLR at page 653, 10 BLC at page 138 and 12 BLC at page 137. 

 13. Advocate Mr. S.M. Rezaul Karim representing the convict-accused-persons Hashem member, Mannan Shah, Salam alias Ketu Salam, Ayesha Begum, Badsha, Faruq Gazi, Jainal Mokter and Shawkat Ali Molla placed his argument in line with the Advocate Mr. Sarwar Ahmed. The learned Advocate wants justice on the basis of convincing and unimpeachable evidence on record. 

 14. Mr. Bhismadev Chakrabarty, the learned Deputy Attorney General representing the State submits that the learned court below was perfectly right in passing the impugned judgment and order which warrants no interference by this court and that the impugned judgment and order should be upheld and confirmed and that the Death Reference should be accepted. The learned Deputy Attorney General further submits that the delay in lodging the FIR has been explained adequately and that the delay should not be accepted as a ritualistic formula; that GDE No. 194 is not the FIR and that if the GDE made first is vague and indefinite, there is no bar to lodge a second FIR; that the FIR is not the encyclopedia and that there is no hard and fast rule that it must contain all the detailed facts of an occurrence; that the prosecution is not required to examine each and every charge sheeted witness and that it is for the prosecution to decide whom it will examine; that the photographs which show of the commission of the offence seized under a Seizure List are proved and that there is no scope to say that those photographs were created mechanically; that the delay in recording the statements under Section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is not fatal to the prosecution in the facts and circumstances of the case inasmuch as every case has different facts and circumstances and that the facts and circumstances of this case is quite distinguishable from the cases referred to by the defence; that the evidence of the partisan or relative witnesses cannot be discarded for their being related to the informant-side; that the Druta Bichar Tribunal, had jurisdiction to try the case inasmuch as the Government by executive order sent the case record to the Tribunal for trial; that the trial of the case was concluded within the stipulated period; that the examination of the accused-persons under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure was not illegality, mere irregularity and that at the time of examination of the accused-persons under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the accused-persons were given advantage to explain their case and as such, it has not affected the case of the prosecution in any way; that the prosecution case is not an absurd one; that admittedly, the occurrence being took place in presence of thousands of people, it is difficult to pinpoint specifically the role played by each and every accused. The learned Deputy Attorney General also referred the decisions reported in 62 DLR (AD) at page 1, 6 MLR (AD) at page 240, 9 BLT (AD) at page 153, 21 BLD (AD) at page 103, 53 DLR (AD) at page 103, 38 DLR at page 289, 43 DLR (AD) at page 44, 1 BLC at page 82, 44 DLR at page 217, 6 MLR (AD) at page 170, 43 DLR (AD) at page 95, 43 DLR (AD) at page 234, 43 DLR at page 87, 42 DLR (AD) at page 31, 54 DLR (AD) at page 146, 42 DLR (AD) at page 171 and 199 SCMR 1668 and 6 MLR (AD) at page 240. 

 16. The P.W.1, the informant Meherunnessa deposed that the occurrence took place on 07.07.2001. At the time of occurrence she was staying at their residence situated at Kathalbari, Sreenagar, District-Munshiganj. On the date of occurrence at about 8 a.m. her husband Manwar Ali, his elder brother Anwar Ali, cousin Badsha, nephew Salauddin and Hashem started for Bagra Bazar with their licensed gun and pistol. When they reached near the house of Tota Sikder, the accused Aiyub Ali, his son Mahfuz, Ayesha Akter, her son Nizam, Nadim, Mizan, Alauddin, Sabuj Ali, Kuti Chand, Mobile Mannan, Manan Shah, Mithu, Shawkat Ali, Jewel, Faruq Gazi, Ketu Salam, Mithun, Hashem, Javed Ali and others attacked Manwar Ali, his brother and nephew. They took shelter in the two storied house of Srijan Ali. The son of the accused Aiyub Ali, Mizan, Nizam and Alauddin entered into the house of Srijan Ali at about 11.00 a.m. to 12.00 O'clock noon. The accused Faruq Gazi shoot Hashem to death. Badsha got injured at the firing of the accused-persons Mannan Shah, Ketu Salam and Mobile Mannan. The accused-persons made hasty efforts to drag Badsha out of the house whereon Manwar Ali opened fire for safety. Manwar Ali made mobile calls to the police station and his relatives and informed them of the occurrence. At about 4.00 p.m. police came to the place of occurrence. By miking police asked Manwar Ali to throw his arms and ammunitions ensuring him to give security. Hearing that, the deceased Manwar Ali threw down his arms. Then, the accused-persons Kuti Chand, Shawkat Ali, Mobile Mannan, Mannan Shah, Ketu Salam and Faruq Gazi put the house on fire from all sides. Thereafter, police asked her husband to come down whereon her husband came down. Police handcuffed her husband, Salauddin, Anwar Ali and Badsha. Police brought them out of the house. The accused-persons Aiyub Ali and the terrorists snatched away Manwar Ali and his brother from police custody. Aiyub Ali dealt chapati blow on the back of the head of Manwar Ali. The accused Kuti Chand dealt wooden 'dasa' blow on the head of the deceased Manwar Ali. The accused-persons Nizam, Mizan, Nadim, Hashem, Mobile Mannan, Mannan Shah dealt iron rod, and sharp cutting weapon blows to her husband resulting in his death. In the same way the aforesaid accused-persons inflicted injuries to Salauddin by dealing sharp cutting blows and left him behind thinking that Salauddin had died. The accused-person Aiyub Ali and the said persons killed Badsha at that place by dealing sharp cutting weapon blows. The accused Aiyub 'Ali and the said accused-persons dealt sharp cutting weapon blows to Anwar Ali, pressed his nose, cut the nails of his hands and left him behind considering that he had died. At about 6.30 p.m. having heard the death news of her husband and others she lost her sense. 15 days after that he heard about the death of Anwar Ali, Hashem and Salauddin. She heard about the occurrence from the witnesses, namely, Nurjahan, Jahanara, Mohammad Ali, Abul Kalam, Shahjahan, Morom Ali, Hanoo, Rezzak and Mosharraf. She got the FIR written by her son who read it over to her. She lodged the FIR on 12.07.2001 in the police station. This witness proved the FIR as Exhibit-1 and her signatures therein as Exhibits-1/1-1/6. This witness further deposed that the road was barricated after the occurrence and that being panicked delay occurred in fling the case. This witness identified the accused-persons Aiyub Ali and Ayesha in the dock. In her cross this witness stated that on the date of occurrence her husband went to the market for purchasing things. After the witnesses narrated the occurrence partly to her, she lost her sense. On the date of occurrence Manwar Ali, Hashem and Badsha died. The house of the accused Aiyub Ali was situated to the west of the place of occurrence. She heard that many police went to the place of occurrence. This witness denied the defence -suggestions that no occurrence as narrated by her took place on the date, at the time and at the place of occurrence or that the accused-persons were not involved in the alleged occurrence or that the accused Aiyub Ali was not present at the time of occurrence or that he was a crippled man at the time of occurrence or that the case was a false one or that she deposed falsely. 

 17. The P.W.2 Alhaj Sirajuddin Bepari alias Srijan Bepari disclosed in his deposition that on the date of occurrence i.e. on 07.07.2001 at 8.00 a.m. to 9.00 a.m. he was sitting in his house. At that time Manwar Ali, Anwar Ali, Badsha, Hashem and Salauddin came to him and addressing him as uncle entreated to save them. On query, he learnt that the accused Aiyub Ali was chasing them to kill. Salauddin forthwith closed the door. He looked through the window to see that the accused Aiyub Ali himself and his associates encircled the north and western side of his house and that they were pelting stones targeting his house. Subsequently, the accused-persons Kuti Chand, Nizam, Nazim, Sabuj Ali, Hashem and Alauddin broke open the door and entered into his house and made attempt to drag away Badsha. Hashem who took shelter in his house was trying to drag Badsha into the house. The accused Faruq Gazi shoot Hashem with a gun. As a result, Hashem fell down on the bags containing paddy. From out side the house, the accused persons fired many shots. The accused Mannan was firing with a cut rifle. The accused Ketu Salam was firing with a gun targeting his house. He saw that the decaeased Badsha was bleeding. Manwar Ali told that Badsha was injured. They took Badsha to the 1st floor. Subsequently, he saw Alauddin to fall down. After taking Badsha to the floor the, deceased Manwar Ali closed the door of the stair case at 11.30 a.m. to 12 O'clock noon. Subsequently, he went out of his house and went to the house of his cousin and saw that firing was going on. Manwar Ali and others were also firing. He heard that the accused Aiyub Ali also opened fire. Thereafter, he heard that the deceased Manwar Ali was being asked to surrender. In the evening police brought down Manwar Ali, Badsha, Anwar Ali and Salauddin under handcuff. When they were brought in front of a bamboo clump the accused Aiyub All dealt sharp cutting blow under his head and asked his associates why they still kept alive those persons. He asked his associates to deal sharp cutting blows to Manwar All and others. Subsequently, the 'other accused-persons namely, Kuti Chand, Mizan, Nazim dealt sharp cutting blows to Manwar All and also beat him up. The accused Kuti Chand had a `wooden rowa(dasa)' in his hand, the accused Nazir had an iron pipe of tube well, the 

 accused Badsha had a 'ciao' in his hand. The accused Mizan had a 'ciao' in his right hand and a rod in his left hand. On perusal of the said GDE, it transpres that S.I. lqbal Bahar Akhand making the GDE started for the place of occurrence with police force simply noting that "turmoil and chasing are taking place" which is simply a routine work of a police officer to go out to any place from police station and according to the provisions of section 154 of the Cr.PC Penal Code, the information must be about a cognizable offence, but in the instant case no offence as instant case has been disclosed in the saide GDE. Moreover the occurrence took place later on i.e. at about 4.00/4.30 p.m. and as such, said GDE cannot be treated as an FIR. It is to be noted further that about the alleged occurrence several First Information Reports were lodged by the men of the accused-side implicating the men of the present informant out of whom the pw2 and the pw3 and the pw4 were seriously injured. Those First Information Reports did not disclose the offence actually disclosed the offence actually occurred, but the instant FIR disclosed the real picture of the offence and when CID investigated into the matter found truth in the instant FIR story, and submitted charge sheet against the accused-persons and Final Reports in other cases. There is no hard and fast rule in taking a subsequent FIR. In the cases of abdul Khaleque versus the State, Abdul Rouf versus the The State and Minhaj and another versus The State and the case of Touhid Alam versus The State reported in 53 DLR (AD) at page 102, 55 DLR at page 202, 21 BLD (AD) at page 103 and 38 DLR at page 289 as referred by the learned DAG our apex court and this court held that there is no bar to file a second FIR; that in view of the vague and indefinite information the lodging of the second FIR is justified. In view of the discussion made so far, this court finds substance in the submission of the learned DAG. 

 56. Advocate Mr. Sarwar Ahmed, Advocate Mr. Md. Shah Manjurul Haque and Advocate Mrs. Hasna Begum next submit that that the statements of the witnesses under section 161 of the Code of Criminal procedure being recorded after a long lapse of time the evidence of the prosecution witnesses should be left out of consideration. The learned Advocates also referred the case of Bangladesh versus Paran Chandra Mondol reported in 6 BCR (AD) at page 225 and the case of State versus Babul Hossain reported in 52 DLR at page 400. In the said cases it is held that long delay in examining the material witnesses cast a doubt on the whole prosecution case and that belated examination of the witnesses by the Investigating Officer for no plausible reason possibility of embellissihing the prosecution case by the witnesses can not be ruled out. 

 59. Advocate Mr. Sarwar Ahmed further submits that the prosecution did not examine all the witnesses named in the FIR and the Charge Sheet which rendered the prosecution case doubtful. In this regard, the learned Advocate referred the case of Muslim Uddin and others versus The State reported in 38 DLR (AD) at page 311. On the otherhand, the learned DAG Mr. Bhismaadeb Chakraborty submits that the prosecution is not bound to examine all the FIR name charge sheeted witnesses. The learned DAG also referred the case of Abdul Hai Sikder and another versus The State reported in 43 DLR (AD) at page 95. In the case reported in 38 DLR (AD) at page 311 our apex court held that an accused is presumed to be innocent of the charge till his guilt is established by legal evidence. In the said case it is also held that no particular number of witnesses is legally required to prove the offence. In the case reported in 43 DLR (AD) at page 95 our apex court held that conviction of an accused can safely be based on the solitary evidence of a witness if his evidence is full, complete and self-contained. In this case the pw2 to the pw8, the eye-witnesses cousistently supported the prosecution case and hence, non-examination of all the FIR named and Charge Sheeted witnesses has not in any way affected the merit of the prosecution case.

 75.
